references.text: The crowd is also divided in their view of Jesus, with some calling him a 'deceiver' (peplamenai), just as the Pharisees here ask if they too are 'led astray'.
The Pharisees express the same contempt for the people who do not know the law, calling them 'cursed' (kataraioi) and 'led astray' (peplamenai), paralleling their question here.
Jesus' opponents again accuse him of being a 'Samaritan demon' and that he is 'leading' (planō) the people astray, reflecting the Pharisees' concern that the disciples are led astray.
John quotes Isaiah saying that God has 'blinded' their eyes and 'hardened' their heart so they cannot see, a direct explanation of why they are 'led astray' (peplamenai) in rejecting Jesus.
Jesus warns that those who kill the disciples will think they are offering service to God, a manifestation of the same 'deception' (planē) the Pharisees fear or display.
Jesus warns directly against 'false messiahs' who will 'lead' (planēsei) many astray, a theme underlying the Pharisees' question about whether the disciples are led astray.
